plain: Proper prep is the single biggest factor in epoxy coating success. Start by cleaning the surface thoroughly to remove dust, oil, grease, and any old coatings, using a degreaser for garage floors especially. Repair cracks and holes with a concrete patch compound and let it cure fully. Next, the concrete needs to be mechanically profiled, typically by diamond grinding, which opens the surface pores so epoxy can bond properly; acid etching is a cheaper but less reliable alternative. After grinding, vacuum thoroughly and check the surface with a moisture test, since epoxy applied over damp concrete will fail or bubble. Finally, make sure the concrete has fully cured, generally at least 28 days for new pours, before applying any coating.

Apps are deliberately designed with variable reward mechanisms, like unpredictable social media likes or notifications, that exploit the same psychological triggers as slot machines, keeping people checking compulsively. Smartphones also consolidate nearly every daily task, communication, work, entertainment, navigation, shopping, into one device, so total screen time naturally accumulates even without any single app being addictive. Social pressure and fear of missing out keep people checking messages and feeds frequently. Boredom and idle moments get filled reflexively with scrolling rather than sitting with discomfort. plain: Helicopters are limited mainly by their rotor physics. As a helicopter moves forward, the advancing rotor blade (moving in the direction of travel) experiences much higher airspeed than the retreating blade (moving against it), since the blade's own rotation adds to or subtracts from the aircraft's forward speed. Push the aircraft fast enough, and the advancing blade tip approaches the speed of sound, causing severe drag and vibration, while the retreating blade can lose so much lift it stalls entirely, a dangerous asymmetry called retreating blade stall. This effectively caps most helicopters around 200 to 250 mph. Airplanes generate lift from fixed wings moving straight through the air with no such rotational asymmetry, letting them fly much faster, including well past the speed of sound in some designs.
